dispatch.summary:
T521 (e92d5085 against 43974477) now meets its acceptance and WEB-18, 64, 97 and 98 and SAVE-8, and the rework fixes every finding from review 1e61ca97.

The P2 is fixed. All four Chromium specs now wait after 자동 진행 정지 until the lock lifts before they read the date. The waits are on 진행 방식 변경 or 자동 진행 시작 being enabled. Both stay disabled while held days are still being shown, because draining keeps clockRunning set: gameActionsBlocked and modeSwitchBlocked both read it, and lock() only clears it in drained(). So these waits really cover the drain. The x1 stop accepts 8월 2–5일. At most 3 days are held, and in-flight plus held never exceeds the depth, so it stays short of the 8월 7일 eve.

The P3s are fixed too:
- A notice read during play is now marked on the shown day and on every held day (withRead). This cannot change which days stop the clock: an unread window-open stop is never on screen while the clock runs.
- A late day is now followed one full interval after it shows: late is when it lands after its turn or the timer fires half an interval late. This matches "one per pace interval" in WEB-18, and the two adjusted beat cases in progression.test.ts check out arithmetically.
- openSlots now calls pause(true), which goes through stop(): held days are shown at once and saved once before slots.sync reads the synchronously published view.

The rest:
- I scanned the other e2e stop sites (intervention, stable-controls, records, native-touch, club-identity, facility-art) and none reads the date mid-drain in a way that would fail.
- The one integration case with automatic commands (client.test.ts autosave) still holds by reading.
- The edits outside touches (App.tsx and the four specs) are scoped and are what the last review asked for.

Evidence: the worker ran typecheck, lint, format:check, the two progression unit files (61 tests) and the --changed unit and contract run (112 tests). Integration and Chromium were left for the coordinator's batch. The remaining items are optional P3s.

findings.message: The guard `daysUntilNextMatch(before) > 4` exists so that the run never reaches the first match day. At level 4 matchEve is off, so nothing stops play at the eve. The owner's stop now shows up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS.x1 = 3 more days after the click. The rested date can therefore move from about 8월 4–6일 to 8월 7–9일, and may play our first match. No assertion breaks (players and currentDay only), but the comment and guard no longer state the real invariant. Either widen the guard to cover the held days (e.g. `> 4 + RUN_AHEAD_DAYS.x1`) or reword the comment.

Both specs dropped their x2 run. Its held days could reach the 8월 7일 eve after an x1 stop that had already moved the date. The titles still say 'advances real days at each speed' and 'advances at the dropdown pace', but the browser now only runs x1 and x10. Optional: run x2 first from 8월 1일, so start plus stop plus 3 held days rests by 8월 5일, or rename the tests. Exact counts are already covered in progression.runahead.test.ts.

findings.message: Two decisions left in T521's result limits are not recorded in the SSOT yet. (1) Reads that skip the command queue are answered from the worker's head. These are head-to-head, club records, archives, person career, league fixtures and manager history. During play they can show one of our results up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS before its day is shown. This is the deferred P3 from the last review. (2) Leaving play for the slot screen now shows held days at once (App.tsx openSlots → pause(true)). WEB-18/98 only name office entry and hiding for that. The worker cannot write STATE or SSOT, so the coordinator should carry both into the STATE inbox or an update-ssot so they are not lost after integration.

reviewHistory.summary: T521's code meets its acceptance. The client keeps held days and shows them in order. Requests start from the newest held day. The controller computes days back to back up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS (x1 3, x2 3, x5 5, x10 7) and computes nothing past a day that stops the clock (new event or decision, critical alert, bankruptcy, observed match eve). The owner's stop shows the held days at the pace, keeps the lock until they are shown, then saves once. Office entry and hiding show held days at once, and a pace change shows held days at the faster pace. The unit suites cover these rules well, and I found no correctness defect in progression.ts or client.ts. Changes are requested for one reason: the new stop shows held days for a few seconds after the owner stops, and several Chromium specs assert the date the moment stop is clicked. They will fail every run (the worker listed them), no task in auto-play-2 owns them, and the group's pre-push batch will be red. The P3 items are optional.

findings.message: T521's owner stop now keeps showing the held days at the pace after the click. At x1 computing a day takes milliseconds, so 3 days are always held, and the stop runs on for about 3 s. These specs will fail every run, not just on slow machines. progression-settings clicks stop right after 8월 2일 and asserts 8월 2일 holds, but the date ends on 8월 5일. recruitment reads `stopped` right after the stop and asserts it is unchanged 1.2 s later. training reads `paused` right after the stop and asserts it much later. season-flow's 400 ms stability poll can settle before the held days finish. The result lists them, but no task in auto-play-2 owns them: T522 only touches scripts/ and reports/. The group's pre-push Chromium batch will fail. Fix: after clicking 자동 진행 정지, wait until 진행 방식 변경 / 자동 진행 시작 is enabled again (the lock lifts when the last held day is shown) before reading the date. Accept 8월 2–5일 for the x1 stop. Where an x2 stop can run on to the 8월 7일 match eve, stop earlier or expect the eve card. These files are outside T521's touches. The coordinator should either widen T521's touches for the resubmission or open a follow-up task that lands before the group's batch.

Reading notifications while days are held only updates the newest held day. The day on screen and the older held days were computed before the read, so they still show the items as unread. For up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS pace intervals (about 3 s at x1), 모두 읽음 and single reads during play look like they did nothing, and the 모두 읽음 button stays enabled. WEB-97 says reading notifications stays usable during play. Consider marking the items read on the shown view and on every held day as well, and add a case to progression.runahead.test.ts.

Every request now starts from the newest held day. That includes reads that skip the queue: head-to-head, club records, archives, person career, league fixtures and manager history. During play these can return one of our match results up to 7 days before its day is shown. This spoils the calendar and disagrees with the shown view's ownMatches. The impl notes accept this from the prototype. If it stays, record it under WEB-18; otherwise have views that mix worker reads with the shown view cut them off at the shown date.

After a day that shows late, the next held day is placed on the pace's beat, 0.5 to 1.5 intervals later. For example, a day 0.6 intervals late puts the next one 1.4 intervals later, even though that day is ready. The acceptance says 'one pace interval after the previous one'. The result discloses this, and it is invisible at x10, but at x1 a day can stay on screen for 0.5 s or 1.4 s. Either set due = now + interval after a late day, or record the beat rule in WEB-18 (update-ssot).

openSlots calls controller.pause(), which now keeps showing held days after the game screen has closed. It then syncs the slot card from the date shown before those days. The save that follows, and any park() checkpoint, hold the later date, so the slot card's date and cash can be several days stale. Consider showing held days at once when leaving play, as entering the office and hiding the tab already do, before slots.sync.

dispatch.summary:
T524 is done. During automatic play, a read that skips the command queue can no longer show results from a day the calendar hasn't reached yet. The edits are in the three touched files plus the task's acceptance checks and result. Nothing is committed.

How it works:
- **One read path.** All nine reads (`archive`, `recruitmentHistory`, `mediationPreview`, `personCareer`, `headToHead`, `clubRecords`, `managerHistory`, `leagueFixtures`, `fullStats`) now go through a single private `read()` in `client.ts`. It asks a gate (`readGate`) first. The progression controller sets that gate when it is created and clears it on dispose.
- **What the gate does while the clock runs.** In `progression.ts`, the read counts as pending, and `compute()` sends no step until it is answered. If a step is in flight, the read waits for it to land. Then every held day is shown at once through `flush()`, the same path as entering the office or hiding the tab. If the owner's stop was still showing days, it ends there, unlocking and saving. Only then is the read sent. Computing ahead resumes as soon as the read is answered or fails. The clock never stops.
- **Otherwise.** With the clock stopped, in manual mode or with the tab hidden, the gate does nothing and the read goes out at once, as before.

Tests: `progression.runahead.test.ts` has 13 new cases. They cover held days shown before a head-to-head read is sent, a read started during an in-flight step, no steps sent until the reply or an error and the run continuing after, a read with nothing held changing nothing, a read during the owner's stop, and all nine reads going out only after the held days are shown. The fake client is now built on `GameClient.prototype`, so these cases exercise the real read path. When I disabled the gate, 12 of the 13 failed; only the nothing-held case passed, which is correct.

Checks run and passing:
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit apps/web/src/runtime/progression.test.ts apps/web/src/runtime/progression.runahead.test.ts` (74 tests)
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit --project contract --changed 53ce730c --passWithNoTests` (8 files, 125 tests). My first try at this one was blocked because I had added `$?` to the command. The plain command then ran and passed.

Left for the batch run (not run here): `pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/web/src/runtime/client.test.ts` and `PREVIEW_BUILD=1 pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium`. `client.test.ts` is untouched because its reads run without a controller.

Behaviour the task text didn't spell out, also listed in the result:
- If the clock runs with nothing held and nothing in flight, the read goes out at once but still pauses computing ahead until it is answered.
- Catch-up steps (hidden tab, or returning after time away) aren't held by reads. Each is shown as it lands, before any read sent behind it is answered.
- A read waiting on an in-flight step leaves the held days showing at the normal pace until that step lands, then shows them all at once.

dispatch.summary:
T521 is implemented, and every task-tier check I ran passes. The integration and e2e runs are left to the batch gate. Four e2e specs are likely to fail there because of the new stop behaviour; I left them unchanged.

**What changed**
- `client.ts`: the client now holds the days automatic play computes, oldest first. The newest one is the head: requests, saves and export start from it, and `reveal()` shows the held days in order. A notice read while days are held updates the newest held day. Any other owner command, a load or a new world is shown at once and clears what was held. The reply handler moved out of the constructor into `received` so it can be unit-tested.
- `progression.ts`: adds `RUN_AHEAD_DAYS` (x1 3, x2 3, x5 5, x10 7). While the page is shown, the controller computes back to back until that many days are held. Each day is shown on the pace's beat, or as soon as it lands when late.
- **Stopping days:** nothing is computed past a day with a new stopping event or pending decision, a critical alert, bankruptcy or a match eve that stops for observation. The clock stops when that day is shown, so the world sits on the shown date.
- **Owner's stop:** the held days are shown at the pace, management stays locked until the last one, then it unlocks and the save is requested once.
- **Show at once:** entering the owner office, hiding the tab and blocker stops show the held days immediately.
- **Hidden or returning:** nothing is computed ahead. Catch-up steps are shown as they land.
- **Pace change:** applies to new days; held days keep the faster of the old and new pace.
- `progression.runahead.test.ts` (new, 14 cases): covers every acceptance scenario plus the real client's hold and reveal. On a modelled x10 run for 30 s it shows no stall and 300 days, against 50 stalls and 175 days computing one day at a time.
- `progression.test.ts`: the 44 existing cases still pass. They now run one day at a time behind a fake client that holds and reveals like the real one.
- `OwnerOfficeView.tsx`: unchanged, because office entry already goes through `enterOffice()`, which now shows held days at once.

**Checks run**
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run format:check` pass.
- The two progression test files pass (58 tests).
- The changed-file unit/contract selection passes: 8 files, 109 tests.

**Not run, left to the batch**
- `client.test.ts` (integration). Reading it, its autosave case should still pass.
- e2e on Chromium. The prototype commits `db28c045`/`b9a6956a` aren't in this repository, so I wrote this from the spec (WEB-18/64/97/98, SAVE-8). The stall test uses modelled step times (25/120/400 ms), not the 261027 trace.

**E2E specs likely to fail** (outside my files, unrun): after a stop, up to 3 more days are now shown at x1/x2, and the first match eve (8월 7일) is close enough to be reached.
- `progression-settings.spec.ts` lines 66–100 expect the date to stay on 8월 2일 after the x1 stop.
- `season-flow.spec.ts` lines 28–58 can read the date before the stop has finished showing days, and the x2 stop may land on the eve.
- `training.spec.ts` lines 136–178 read the date right after the stop. A slow page can reach the eve, and restarting then plays round 1.
- `recruitment.spec.ts` lines 365–368 read the date right after the stop.

Waiting for 자동 진행 시작 to become enabled before reading the date fixes the reads. The eve cases need an earlier stop or should expect the eve. All of this is recorded in the task result limits.

dispatch.summary:
The blocking review finding (P2) is fixed, along with three of the four optional P3 items. The fixes are in four Chromium specs and `App.tsx`, all outside T521's listed touches, so the scope check may flag them. I have not run them; client.test.ts and the Chromium specs are left for the batch gate.

**P2 — specs that read the date right after 자동 진행 정지**
- `progression-settings.spec.ts`: after the x1 stop it waits for 진행 방식 변경 to be enabled, then accepts 8월 2–5일 and checks the date holds. I dropped the x2 stop: its held days can reach the 8월 7일 match eve, and pressing play there plays the match through.
- `season-flow.spec.ts`: waits for 자동 진행 시작 to be enabled instead of the 400 ms stability polls. The x2 stop is dropped for the same eve reason.
- `training.spec.ts`: stops as soon as 훈련 shows the clock still running, then waits for play to be enabled. That keeps the held days short of the first match eve, so round 1 is not played.
- `recruitment.spec.ts`: waits for play to be enabled before reading `stopped`.
- The other specs that click stop already wait for something the lock gates or don't depend on the date, so I left them unchanged.

**P3 items**
- **Read marks:** a notice read while days are held now shows as read on the day on screen and on every held day, not just the newest. This is in `client.ts`.
- **Late days:** a day that shows late is now followed by the next one a full pace interval later, instead of on the next beat. This matches the acceptance wording. In the one-day-at-a-time suite this changed two timing expectations in `progression.test.ts`, which I updated.
- **Slot screen:** opening the slot screen now shows the held days at once (`pause(true)`), so the slot card and the save hold the same date. This is the `App.tsx` change.
- **Not changed (left for the planner):** reads that skip the command queue (head-to-head, club records, archives, person career, league fixtures, manager history) answer from the newest computed day, so during play they can show one of our results up to 7 days early. Either recording that under WEB-18 or cutting those views at the shown date is a spec decision; it's in the result limits.

**Checks run, all passing:** `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`; the two progression test files (61 passed); the changed-file unit/contract selection against 8fa61603 (8 files, 112 passed). The modelled 30 s x10 run now shows 0 stalls and 300 days, against 44 stalls and 157 days computing one day at a time.

**Not run, for the batch:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/web/src/runtime/client.test.ts` and `PREVIEW_BUILD=1 pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium`, which includes the four edited specs.

The task result in `spec/tasks/T521.run-ahead-clock.md` is updated with all of this.

review.summary:
T521 (e92d5085 against 43974477) now meets its acceptance and WEB-18, 64, 97 and 98 and SAVE-8, and the rework fixes every finding from review 1e61ca97.

The P2 is fixed. All four Chromium specs now wait after 자동 진행 정지 until the lock lifts before they read the date. The waits are on 진행 방식 변경 or 자동 진행 시작 being enabled. Both stay disabled while held days are still being shown, because draining keeps clockRunning set: gameActionsBlocked and modeSwitchBlocked both read it, and lock() only clears it in drained(). So these waits really cover the drain. The x1 stop accepts 8월 2–5일. At most 3 days are held, and in-flight plus held never exceeds the depth, so it stays short of the 8월 7일 eve.

The P3s are fixed too:
- A notice read during play is now marked on the shown day and on every held day (withRead). This cannot change which days stop the clock: an unread window-open stop is never on screen while the clock runs.
- A late day is now followed one full interval after it shows: late is when it lands after its turn or the timer fires half an interval late. This matches "one per pace interval" in WEB-18, and the two adjusted beat cases in progression.test.ts check out arithmetically.
- openSlots now calls pause(true), which goes through stop(): held days are shown at once and saved once before slots.sync reads the synchronously published view.

The rest:
- I scanned the other e2e stop sites (intervention, stable-controls, records, native-touch, club-identity, facility-art) and none reads the date mid-drain in a way that would fail.
- The one integration case with automatic commands (client.test.ts autosave) still holds by reading.
- The edits outside touches (App.tsx and the four specs) are scoped and are what the last review asked for.

Evidence: the worker ran typecheck, lint, format:check, the two progression unit files (61 tests) and the --changed unit and contract run (112 tests). Integration and Chromium were left for the coordinator's batch. The remaining items are optional P3s.

findings.message: The guard `daysUntilNextMatch(before) > 4` exists so that the run never reaches the first match day. At level 4 matchEve is off, so nothing stops play at the eve. The owner's stop now shows up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS.x1 = 3 more days after the click. The rested date can therefore move from about 8월 4–6일 to 8월 7–9일, and may play our first match. No assertion breaks (players and currentDay only), but the comment and guard no longer state the real invariant. Either widen the guard to cover the held days (e.g. `> 4 + RUN_AHEAD_DAYS.x1`) or reword the comment.

Both specs dropped their x2 run. Its held days could reach the 8월 7일 eve after an x1 stop that had already moved the date. The titles still say 'advances real days at each speed' and 'advances at the dropdown pace', but the browser now only runs x1 and x10. Optional: run x2 first from 8월 1일, so start plus stop plus 3 held days rests by 8월 5일, or rename the tests. Exact counts are already covered in progression.runahead.test.ts.

findings.message: Two decisions left in T521's result limits are not recorded in the SSOT yet. (1) Reads that skip the command queue are answered from the worker's head. These are head-to-head, club records, archives, person career, league fixtures and manager history. During play they can show one of our results up to RUN_AHEAD_DAYS before its day is shown. This is the deferred P3 from the last review. (2) Leaving play for the slot screen now shows held days at once (App.tsx openSlots → pause(true)). WEB-18/98 only name office entry and hiding for that. The worker cannot write STATE or SSOT, so the coordinator should carry both into the STATE inbox or an update-ssot so they are not lost after integration.

dispatch.summary:
T524 is done. During automatic play, a read that skips the command queue can no longer show results from a day the calendar hasn't reached yet. The edits are in the three touched files plus the task's acceptance checks and result. Nothing is committed.

How it works:
- **One read path.** All nine reads (`archive`, `recruitmentHistory`, `mediationPreview`, `personCareer`, `headToHead`, `clubRecords`, `managerHistory`, `leagueFixtures`, `fullStats`) now go through a single private `read()` in `client.ts`. It asks a gate (`readGate`) first. The progression controller sets that gate when it is created and clears it on dispose.
- **What the gate does while the clock runs.** In `progression.ts`, the read counts as pending, and `compute()` sends no step until it is answered. If a step is in flight, the read waits for it to land. Then every held day is shown at once through `flush()`, the same path as entering the office or hiding the tab. If the owner's stop was still showing days, it ends there, unlocking and saving. Only then is the read sent. Computing ahead resumes as soon as the read is answered or fails. The clock never stops.
- **Otherwise.** With the clock stopped, in manual mode or with the tab hidden, the gate does nothing and the read goes out at once, as before.

Tests: `progression.runahead.test.ts` has 13 new cases. They cover held days shown before a head-to-head read is sent, a read started during an in-flight step, no steps sent until the reply or an error and the run continuing after, a read with nothing held changing nothing, a read during the owner's stop, and all nine reads going out only after the held days are shown. The fake client is now built on `GameClient.prototype`, so these cases exercise the real read path. When I disabled the gate, 12 of the 13 failed; only the nothing-held case passed, which is correct.

Checks run and passing:
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit apps/web/src/runtime/progression.test.ts apps/web/src/runtime/progression.runahead.test.ts` (74 tests)
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit --project contract --changed 53ce730c --passWithNoTests` (8 files, 125 tests). My first try at this one was blocked because I had added `$?` to the command. The plain command then ran and passed.

Left for the batch run (not run here): `pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/web/src/runtime/client.test.ts` and `PREVIEW_BUILD=1 pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium`. `client.test.ts` is untouched because its reads run without a controller.

Behaviour the task text didn't spell out, also listed in the result:
- If the clock runs with nothing held and nothing in flight, the read goes out at once but still pauses computing ahead until it is answered.
- Catch-up steps (hidden tab, or returning after time away) aren't held by reads. Each is shown as it lands, before any read sent behind it is answered.
- A read waiting on an in-flight step leaves the held days showing at the normal pace until that step lands, then shows them all at once.
